elements.quote: There is limited evidence to evaluate the sustainability of evidence-based interventions (EBIs) for healthcare improvement.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly describes the current state of knowledge (limited evidence) and uncertainties (unclear which approach is most effective).

elements.quote: It is unclear which approach/approaches are most effective for evaluating sustainability and what measures and outcomes are most commonly used. There is a disconnect between evaluating the factors that may shape sustainability and the outcomes approaches employed to measure sustainability. Our review offers methodological recommendations for sustainability evaluation research and highlights the importance in understanding mechanisms of sustainability to advance the field.
elements.reason: The abstract explains the importance and need for the review by highlighting the disconnect in current research and the value of the review's recommendations.

elements.quote: A focus on evaluation is what differentiates this review from recent syntheses published on approaches to sustainability research.
elements.reason: The discussion explains the need for the current review by differentiating it from recent syntheses and citing previous work (e.g., Lennox et al.) to justify the specific focus on evaluation approaches.
This is an integrative review of evaluation approaches, not a review of intervention effects, so the requirement to describe the mechanism of action of the intervention does not apply.
The review is an integrative review of evaluation approaches rather than a primary study of complex interventions, and no logic model is presented in the rationale.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare.
elements.reason: The review explicitly states its objective in the Aim section, clearly defining the scope of the review.

elements.quote: The aim of this integrative review was to identify and synthesize approaches that have been used to evaluate the sustainability of EBIs in healthcare.
elements.reason: The review focuses on identifying evaluation approaches rather than assessing intervention effects, making PICO comparisons not applicable.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal • Were primary research • Had explicit research design and data collection methods • Had an explicit theoretical approach... • Were within a healthcare setting • Evaluated the sustainability of an EBI
elements.reason: Table 1 specifies study design (primary research), setting (healthcare), and topic (sustainability of EBI) characteristics used for eligibility.

elements.quote: Articles were included if they: • Were published in a peer-review journal
elements.reason: Table 1 specifies publication status (peer-review) and text_21 specifies language (English) and search dates imply dissemination year criteria.

elements.quote: Articles were excluded if they: ... Did not evaluate the sustainability of an EBI or QI intervention using a defined approach or, Did not evaluate sustainability using a clear research design and method
elements.reason: The exclusion criteria do not distinguish between exclusion due to outcomes not measured versus outcome results not reported.
The Methods section does not specify how studies were grouped for syntheses, only the results of the grouping are described in the Results section.

elements.quote: We only included published studies in the English language and peer-reviewed primary studies in this review.
elements.reason: The text states the restrictions but does not provide rationales for why these restrictions were applied.

elements.quote: In December 2018 and July 2020, we searched the following databases
elements.reason: The text explicitly reports the dates (December 2018 and July 2020) when the information sources were last searched.

elements.reason: The Discussion section explicitly compares the review's findings to other recent syntheses and specific studies (e.g., Lennox et al.), stating that findings are consistent with other work, thus interpreting results in the context of other evidence.

elements.quote: While qualitative research designs gather rich detail on potential determinants of sustainability (e.g., context) and participant's perspectives on the sustainability process, this design cannot solely measure mechanisms and outcomes of sustainability.
elements.reason: The Discussion section explicitly discusses limitations of the evidence included in the review, noting that the predominant qualitative study designs cannot solely measure mechanisms and outcomes.

elements.quote: We only included published studies in the English language and peer-reviewed primary studies in this review. This review entailed a comprehensive search of published literature and rigorous review methods; however, we recognize that there is the possibility of incomplete retrieval of identified research. For example, all gray literature was excluded.
elements.reason: The authors explicitly discuss limitations of the review process, including language restrictions, peer-review requirements, and exclusion of gray literature.
